To both parties: the recommended route for this trip was 8.2 km and the driver's recorded distance was 9.4 km, a deviation of 1.20 km. That is above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22, so the deviation is established on the platform's recorded distances, and the GPS trace confirms the shape of it (PIE, then Bedok North Road from 09:26:25, Upper Changi Road from 09:30:25, rejoining Still Road at 09:33:55) without being used to re-measure distance. On traffic justification, the only advisory for the recommended PIE segment (Bedok North Road to Still Road, towards Tuas) overlapping the trip window is type NONE, with no incident, roadwork or closure; POL-RD-23 requires congestion, an incident or a closure intersecting the recommended route, so the reroute was not traffic-justified, and the driver's statement that the PIE stretch 'always crawl[s]' is an assertion with nothing in the record behind it. On notification, the chat log holds only the two pickup messages at 09:17:50 and 09:18:15, both before the trip started at 09:19:25, the trip record's messages_during_trip is empty and there are no in-app calls, so under POL-RD-21 the driver did not inform the rider before or at the point the deviation began at 09:26:44, and any unrecorded verbal notice cannot be established (POL-GEN-26). Applying POL-RD-24, row (d) governs: a deviation over 1 km that is not traffic-justified, refunding the excess distance fare in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate: 1.20 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.10 SGD, without surge and rounded to the cent, matching the payments ledger's own derived figure. The rider asked for 4.00 SGD, but the policy's measure of the disputed distance is the excess distance fare and no more, so 1.10 SGD is returned and the remainder of the metered charge (base fare 3.80, distance fare 8.65, time fare 4.08, platform fee 0.90, total charged 17.43) stands. The driver's point that the no-refund rows are not reached, and the rider's point that the case runs on row (d) at 1.10 SGD, are both accepted; both sides' figures on the excess distance fare agree. Ruling: PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.10 SGD to the rider.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

This ruling is read from your claim against the record, rider R-33069, since you filed it. You are owed nothing, so the present state stands and the metered fare of SGD 6.65 stays as charged.

The facts are not seriously in dispute. The platform's recorded distances put the trip at 2.6 km actual against 2.2 km recommended, a deviation of 0.40 km (EV-TRIP-06002, POL-RD-22). The driver-device trace (13 fixes at 30 s, 100.0% coverage, no gap of 120 s or more, EV-GPS-06002) confirms the vehicle left the recommended road at Bukit Batok Central / Bukit Batok East Avenue 3 and rejoined at Jurong East Street 21, so the deviation happened and the driver, D-72866, accepts a deviation in substance.

The controlling clause is POL-RD-24, which says exactly one row applies. The deviation of 0.40 km is 1.0 km or less, so it is within POL-RD-22's tolerance. That leaves two rows: row (c) (traffic-justified, rider not informed, 1 km or less) and row (e) (not traffic-justified, 1 km or less). Both prescribe no refund. The LTA traffic record for the recommended segment of Bukit Batok Road, both directions, over the trip window 15:12-16:42, is type NONE - no incident, no roadwork, no closure, speed bands 5-6 throughout (EV-ADVIS-06002-01). On POL-RD-23 that does not justify the reroute and does not corroborate the roadwork barrier the driver asserted, so the case falls in row (e). Either way, no refund issues.

The driver's failure to inform you is real: the chat log is empty (0 messages, contiguous) and the trip record carries no in-app calls (EV-CHAT-06002), so POL-RD-21's notice obligation was not met and the driver's stated reason is contradicted by the only traffic data on file. But under POL-RD-24 that omission does not change the outcome, because rows (c) and (e) turn on the length of the deviation, not on whether the rider was told. It is recorded here as the reason the driver's account of the trip is not accepted.

Rider's claim for the excess-distance fare. You ask, in the alternative, for the SGD 0.29 the platform computes as the excess-distance fare (0.40 km x 0.72 SGD per km, EV-FARE-06002). POL-RD-24 awards the excess-distance fare only in rows (b) and (d), and both require a deviation over 1.0 km. At 0.40 km this trip is in the tolerance rows, which return no refund, so this claim is rejected on the clause's own terms. Your opening figure of SGD 1.50 is not a sum POL-RD-24 provides, as you acknowledged.

Rider's escalation request. You ask that the tolerance not be read to immunise a reroute with no recognised trigger and no notice, and that if it is, the case go to a human under POL-GEN-26. POL-GEN-26 escalates where a fact a rule needs cannot be established because the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired. Nothing needed here is missing or impaired: the trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown, both profiles and the traffic advisory all carry admissibility status COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The deviation distance, the traffic question and the notification question are each established on the record. POL-GEN-26 therefore does not fire, and POL-RD-24's tolerance rows are the rule this case answers to. No referral arises: the route-deviation policy carries no referral clause in this version.

Outcome for the filing party: your claim is not supported, no money moves, and the SGD 6.65 fare stands as charged with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: this is decided on the platform's own records, and the rider's claim is not supported. The present state stands.

The deviation is real, and I accept it. POL-RD-22 measures it from the trip record's recorded distances, not from the trace: 16.80 km actual less 15.30 km recommended is 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. Both sides agree on this, and the GPS trace (which measures only 14.177 km) is not used to re-measure, exactly as POL-RD-22 provides.

The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. LTA advisory LTA-TI-260923-1113 records an ACCIDENT on the East Coast Parkway (towards Changi) after the Marine Parade exit, valid 17:34:22 to 18:49:22, and so overlapping the trip window (17:49:22 to 18:18:22). ACCIDENT is an admissible 'incident' type. The advisory's road (ECP), direction (towards Changi) and location (after Marine Parade exit) place it on the recommended route's ECP segment, which the recommended route uses from Raffles Avenue through to Bedok South Road; the recommended route does not leave the ECP until Bedok South Road, so an incident after the Marine Parade exit lies on it. The artifact leaves intersection 'undetermined' for the Judge, and on these fields I decide it intersects. The rider's point that the message says 'avoid lanes 2 and 3' does not change this: POL-RD-23 asks whether the advisory intersects the route and shows an incident, not whether the road was impassable.

The driver informed the rider before the deviation, and the rider agreed. MSG-06003-003 was sent at 17:55:39 and read at 17:55:48; MSG-06003-004, 'Sure no problem', was sent at 17:56:14; the route_deviation_detected event is at 17:58:49. POL-RD-21's notice was therefore given before the point of deviation, and the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, so the deviation is agreed.

On POL-RD-24 exactly one row applies, and it is row (a): traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — no refund. Rows (b) and (d) are the refund rows and neither applies. The rider's stated figure of 5.00 SGD is unsupported in any event: the only refund the matrix ever yields is the excess distance fare, which on these figures would be 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, with no surge. The rider filed this dispute, so under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is read against her claim and leaves the metered fare of 26.04 SGD charged and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 undisturbed; it restores nothing to the driver.

The rider's alternative — that the traffic element is unestablished and the case must be escalated under POL-GEN-26 — fails. The fact POL-RD-23 needs is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight_multiplier 1.0 (EV-ADVIS-06003-01), and it is established from that artifact's own fields; there is no missing or impaired evidence and so no open question. POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence requirement is met at 0.85, and POL-GEN-22 (5.00 SGD contested, below the 10.00 SGD band, no fraud flags) permits the AI ruling to stand.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

The rider's claim is partly right and partly overstated. The recommended route for TRP-06004 was 13.1 km and the trip was driven 14.8 km (EV-TRIP-06004), leaving the recommended Seletar Expressway (SLE) at the Woodlands Avenue 12 exit at 08:23:17 and rejoining at Yishun Avenue 2 at 08:32:21; the 45-fix trace (EV-GPS-06004) matches that route, and POL-RD-22 requires the platform's recorded distances to measure the deviation. The deviation is therefore 14.8 - 13.1 = 1.70 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance, so a refund row of POL-RD-24 applies and the tolerance rows (c) and (e) do not.

Notice of the deviation (POL-RD-21): the chat log EV-CHAT-06004 holds only the driver's 08:10:23 arrival message and the rider's 08:10:38 'ok', both before the 08:11:43 start; trip_record.derived.v7.messages_during_trip is empty and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty. The driver did not inform the rider before or at the point of deviation, so row (a) ('informed and agreed') cannot apply.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23): the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-06004-01 is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC record for the SLE 'towards TPE' covering the stretch from the Woodlands Avenue 12 exit to the Yishun Avenue 2 exit - the same two junctions the trip record uses for this deviation - and it overlaps the trip window (07:46:43-09:01:43 against 08:11:43-08:33:43, overlaps_trip_window true). On its road, direction and location it does intersect the recommended route, so the reroute is traffic-justified and row (b) applies. The argument that the advisory is not tied to the recommended route is not accepted on that location description.

The amount is the same either way: rows (b) and (d) both return the excess distance fare alone, and no row of POL-RD-24 returns any part of the trip fare. The excess distance fare is 1.70 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.22 SGD with no surge (thresholds.excess_distance_fare.surge_applied is false), which is also the figure the payments ledger carries (EV-FARE-06004, excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.22).

So of the 3.80 SGD the rider asked for, 1.22 SGD is returned and the balance of the fare stands; the driver is not owed any payment.

Confidence: every artifact carrying these facts (EV-TRIP-06004, EV-GPS-06004, EV-CHAT-06004, EV-FARE-06004, EV-ADVIS-06004-01) is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The contested amount is 3.80 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so the AI ruling is final; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, so no 0.95 uplift; POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar is met and its 2 km ceiling is not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false) and would not bite on a 1.70 km deviation. No referral clause applies to a route deviation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: the rider's dispute is partly upheld. The recorded route distances show the driver travelled 11.5 km against a recommended 9.9 km — a deviation of 1.60 km — which is over the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22, so this is not a within-tolerance case. The driver did not inform the rider of the reroute: the trip's chat log carries 0 messages and there are no in-app calls or call recordings in the record, so under POL-RD-21 the deviation was not notified and not agreed. On traffic justification, POL-RD-23 admits only congestion, an incident or a closure shown by traffic data that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The advisory covering the very KPE segment the driver left (EV-ADVIS-06006-01, Hougang Avenue 2 exit to PIE) is type NONE — no incident, roadwork or closure, speed bands 5-6 throughout. The only advisory of an admissible kind (EV-ADVIS-06006-02) is an ACCIDENT on Upper Serangoon Road near Kovan MRT, a road that appears nowhere on the recommended route (Rivervale Crescent, Sengkang East Road, KPE, PIE, Eunos Road 8), so it does not intersect the recommended route and does not justify this reroute. The driver's account that the KPE was jammed and an accident was shown is a bare assertion; POL-RD-23 says an assertion of traffic with no such data on the route does not justify the reroute. The POL-RD-24 matrix therefore lands on row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare in full. On the recorded figures that is 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.15 SGD, without surge, exactly the excess_distance_fare_sgd the fare record derives. The rider asked for 3.00 SGD, but the policy's measure of this wrong is the excess distance fare only, so 1.15 SGD is returned and the balance of the claim is not granted. The driver's advocate argued the traffic question is unresolvable and the case should escalate; it is resolvable — the traffic data for the recommended route segment shows nothing — and the rider's alternative path (row (b), traffic-justified but uninformed) also yields the same 1.15 SGD, so the amount does not depend on that question. All artifacts relied on (trip record, chat log, fare breakdown and the two traffic advisories) are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0; the contested value of 3.00 SGD is below the 10.00 SGD threshold at which POL-GEN-22 makes an AI ruling final; neither profile carries a fraud flag; and POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence floor is met, so no escalation is required. No referral arises on a route deviation in this policy version.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Rider and driver: the 1.01 SGD refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings on 28 September 2026 is held where it is, and the case goes to a human reviewer. An escalation issues no monetary outcome for either of you and returns nothing to the driver now.

The deviation and the money are settled. The actual route was 14.80 km against a recommended 13.40 km, a deviation of 1.40 km (POL-RD-22) — over the 1.00 km tolerance, so this cannot be closed as within tolerance. The excess distance fare is 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD per km, with no surge, = 1.01 SGD, the exact sum the fare ledger (EV-FARE-06007) shows refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver at 10:33:23.

The traffic question (driver's first claim — accepted). The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-06007-01) records an ACCIDENT on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Adam Road exit, valid 08:35 to 09:48, which covers the trip window of 08:48 to 09:16. On this trip the recommended route stays on the PIE past Adam Road to Clementi Road, and the vehicle was travelling west on the PIE towards Tuas, so the advisory lies on the recommended route and under POL-RD-23 the reroute is traffic-justified. The rider's point that the file leaves the intersection 'undetermined' does not change the outcome: if that were left unresolved, POL-GEN-26 would escalate the case anyway.

The notice question (driver's second claim — accepted as to notice). The driver sent his in-app message at 09:00:37 ('Sir, accident on PIE after Adam Road, I exit Adam Rd and go Holland Road, ok?'), delivered 09:00:40 and read 09:01:20, and the vehicle only left the recommended route at 09:03:37, so he did inform the rider before the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. But the rider answered at 09:01:12 ('Please don't, stay on PIE') and repeated it at 09:05:17, so the deviation was not agreed.

Why no refund row applies. The matrix in POL-RD-24 (v2.1 1.3) has no row for this case. Row (a) needs the rider to have been informed AND to have agreed — she did not agree. Row (b) needs the rider not to have been informed — she was informed. Rows (c) and (e) are for a deviation of 1.00 km or less — this one is 1.40 km. Row (d) needs the reroute not to be traffic-justified — on this record it was. POL-RD-24 says in terms that a case fitting no row — 'informed but the rider objected' — is escalated under POL-GEN-26, and that is this case.

The rider's claims that rows (b) or (d) already send the 1.01 SGD to the rider, and that the driver recovers nothing either way, are rejected on their premise: on these facts the rider was informed and the reroute was justified, so neither row (b) nor row (d) is reached. The rider's GPS point (EV-GPS-06007, POL-RD-22) and excess-fare point (1.01 SGD) are accepted, as is the rider's reading that the driver deviated in the face of a read objection — that is precisely why the case fits no row. The driver's fifth claim (the money is bounded at 1.01 SGD) is accepted.

Open question for the human reviewer: whether a traffic-justified reroute taken after a timely notice but over the rider's express objection should leave the 1.01 SGD with the rider or return it to the driver.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

For the driver (D-28347) and the rider (R-59266) — trip TRP-06005, dispute DSP-06005, category ROUTE_DEVIATION.

What was charged. The trip ran 13.8 km against a recommended 12.4 km, so the deviation is 1.40 km (POL-RD-22: actual 13.8 minus optimal 12.4, the platform's recorded distances). That is above the 1.0 km tolerance, so the rows that excuse a short deviation (POL-RD-24 rows (c) and (e)) cannot apply.

Traffic. I accept the driver's point here. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-06005-01) records a VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Braddell Road exit, valid 18:54:21–20:02:41, which overlaps the whole trip window; the CTE is the road the recommended route uses and 'towards SLE' is the direction of travel, so the advisory intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window (POL-RD-23). The reroute was therefore traffic-justified, and the driver's stated reason (a CTE breakdown) matches it.

Notice to the rider. That is not enough to decide this case. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider by in-app chat (or a recorded call) before or at the point of deviation, and it says a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established. The record shows the notice came after the deviation: the vehicle left the recommended route at the CTE / Balestier Road exit at 19:21:30 (route_deviation_detected), while the driver's first message about it, MSG-06005-003 ('Boss, CTE got breakdown, I already come out at Thomson, will be faster'), is timestamped 19:24:10 — about two minutes forty seconds later. The driver's claim to have told the rider before he left the CTE is contradicted by those timestamps, and the trip record's in_app_calls is empty, so no earlier verbal notice can be established. The rider's 'Ok' at 19:24:50 is an acknowledgment in the chat log, and POL-RD-21 treats an acknowledgment as agreement — but POL-RD-24 row (a) requires the rider to have been informed as well as to have agreed, and the notice the clause requires (before or at the deviation) was not given. Row (a) therefore does not apply, and the refund rows do: row (b) (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km) returns the excess distance fare, and row (d) would return the same amount, so the traffic question does not change the outcome. The driver's compensation claim follows from row (a) and fails with it.

The money. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.40 km × 1.05 SGD = 1.47 SGD (POL-RD-24; per_km_rate_sgd 1.05 from the fare breakdown). That is exactly the 1.47 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (fare_adjusted at 19:50:11; payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED; refund_issued_sgd 1.47). The present state is therefore the remedy the matrix itself produces, so the driver's claim fails. Ruling NO_ACTION: the rider keeps the 1.47 SGD, and no further money moves.

The rider's later statement (that he was told only after the CTE) is consistent with the timestamps, but it is the platform's chat log that decides the notice and the acknowledgment (POL-RD-21), and the log shows a late notice. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-06005) is consistent with the route taken and the timing and does not change this.

The AI decides this finally: the contested value is 1.47 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag; and the 0.80 confidence POL-RD-25 sets for a route deviation is met. Nothing the ruling needs is unestablished, so POL-GEN-26 does not escalate; no safety indicator appears, so POL-GEN-21 does not apply; and a route deviation produces no referral in this version. Confidence is 0.85, within the 1.0 cap set by the artifacts (all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

The rider filed this dispute, so the outcome is read against the rider's claim on trip TRP-06009.

How far the driver went off route (POL-RD-22). POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's own recorded distances, not from the sparse GPS trace. The record gives 34.80 km actual against 32.40 km recommended — a deviation of 2.40 km. The tolerance is 1.00 km, so this detour is more than double it. The within-tolerance 'no refund' rows of the refund matrix are therefore closed to the driver, and this is common ground between the parties.

Was the reroute traffic-justified (POL-RD-23). Yes. The platform-retrieved LTA advisory LTA-TI-260929-3650 records an ACCIDENT on the Ayer Rajah Expressway towards Tuas, after the Lower Delta Road exit, valid 11:01:14 to 12:16:14, which encloses the trip window 11:16:14 to 11:56:14. ACCIDENT is an admissible incident type. The recommended route runs on the AYE and the trip was heading towards Tuas; the vehicle left the AYE at the Lower Delta Road exit at 11:45:45 and rejoined at the Portsdown Road slip road at 11:53:23. The incident, on the AYE just past the Lower Delta Road exit in the direction of travel, lies on exactly the stretch the driver bypassed, so the advisory intersects the recommended route the driver left. I reject the rider's alternative reading that the traffic limb is unproven — the advisory's own road, direction and location, read against the trip, place it there. In any event the point does not change the money: rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 return the same sum.

Was the rider told (POL-RD-21). No. The chat log holds two messages (11:14:04 and 11:14:54), both before the trip started and both about the pick-up, not a detour; the trip record shows no messages during the trip and no call recordings; and the driver's own statement — 'Didn't want to disturb the passenger, he was on his laptop' — is a concession that he gave no notice. POL-RD-21 requires notice before or at the point of deviation, and a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established (POL-GEN-26). Notice is not made out, the rider never agreed, and row (a) is unavailable.

What is owed (POL-RD-24, POL-GEN-03). The case sits in row (b): traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km. The matrix refunds the excess distance fare — the deviation distance times the metered per-km rate, without surge: 2.40 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 2.21 SGD, which is the fare ledger's own excess_distance_fare_sgd figure. The rider asked for 30.00 SGD of the 51.32 SGD fare, but POL-RD-24 provides only the excess distance fare; the metered fare was computed on the recorded 34.80 km and 40.0 minutes and the matrix does not return the whole trip fare. So of the 30.00 SGD contested, 2.21 SGD is owed, as a PARTIAL_REFUND. The fare is confirmed CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider still carries this sum.

Why the ruling can stand (POL-RD-25, POL-GEN-22, POL-GEN-02). No artifact the ruling relies on is impaired — the trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger and LTA advisory are each COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so nothing caps confidence below the bar. The dispute value of 30.00 SGD sits in POL-GEN-22's 10.00 to 50.00 band, requiring a confidence of 0.80, and no fraud flag is carried on either profile to raise it to 0.95. The 2.0 km limb of v2.1 6.2 is held and not applied (thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false), so the 2.40 km deviation does not force escalation.

No referral is produced: a route deviation has no referral clause in this version.

Under POL-GEN-22, a dispute value above POL-GEN-22's second band. The AI prepared the case file -- both advocates were asked -- and no ruling is issued, so the dispute is escalated to a human reviewer with both amounts null and no referral. The reason code is V7_HUMAN_ONLY.

Under POL-GEN-21, the dispute carries dispute.safety_flag, and POL-GEN-21 makes a flagged dispute a person's whatever the category and whatever the value. The AI prepared the case file -- both advocates were asked -- and no ruling is issued, so the dispute is escalated to a human reviewer with both amounts null and no referral. The reason code is V7_HUMAN_ONLY.

Both accounts agree on the essentials, and the records confirm them. The trip deviated 1.90 km from the recommended route (25.10 km actual minus 23.20 km recommended, EV-TRIP-06008; POL-RD-22), above the 1.0 km tolerance. The driver told you in-app before the turn — MSG-06008-003 at 18:42:36, about three minutes before the deviation was logged at 18:45:16 — giving a reason (an accident on the PIE near Bedok) and the alternative roads, and you agreed, 'ok, thanks' (MSG-06008-004); so the deviation was notified and acknowledged (POL-RD-21). The fare charged was 39.98 SGD; the deviation-related part of it is the excess distance fare, 1.90 x 0.92 = 1.75 SGD (POL-RD-24), against the 6.50 SGD the rider contests. The case turns on whether traffic justified the reroute, and that cannot be established. POL-RD-23 makes traffic data for the recommended route at the trip time the only thing that can justify a reroute, and the platform's LTA traffic-feed request for this window failed and was not retried, so EV-ADVIS-06008-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no fact (POL-GEN-02). The record is silent on the PIE at that hour, and that silence is not a finding that there was no accident. The driver's 'I saw it on the map' is an assertion without data, and POL-RD-23 says an assertion alone does not justify a reroute — so the driver cannot win on his own say-so. But the rider's contrary reading fails too: POL-RD-23 shows the driver has not proved justification; it does not establish that no traffic existed. Because the traffic question is undetermined, no row of POL-RD-24 fits — row (a) needs the reroute traffic-justified and row (d) needs it not traffic-justified, and neither is shown — and POL-GEN-26 is explicit that a fact a rule needs (it names 'whether traffic justified the reroute') that cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is missing escalates the case, with no outcome inferred from the absence. On who may decide: the contested value is 6.50 SGD (POL-GEN-22's final band), with no fraud flag, no safety flag and a 1.90 km deviation under the unapplied 2.0 km limb, but POL-RD-25 requires 0.80 confidence for a route-deviation ruling and the missing traffic artifact caps confidence at 0.0, so the AI ruling cannot stand. Outcome: ESCALATE. The 6.50 SGD is held — neither refunded to the rider nor retained by the driver — until a human reviewer resolves the traffic question; the reviewer should have the platform retry the LTA traffic-feed request for the recommended PIE segment over the trip window (2026-09-27, about 18:29-19:05). No referral applies: a route deviation has no referral clause in this version.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
The rider filed this dispute, and the outcome is read from the rider's claim against the record.

What the record establishes. The platform's recorded distances put the actual route at 21.5 km against a recommended 20.4 km — a deviation of 1.10 km (POL-RD-22) — and the tolerance is 1.0 km, so this deviation is outside tolerance and the refund matrix is engaged. Both recorded distances are present and clean, so the deviation is established on the trip record, not on the sparse trace (which measures only 18.171 km over 69 fixes and is expressly not used to re-measure distance).
